claims.text: Chain a single turn (a one-participant round). Convenience over :func:`append_round`; prefer the round form so ordering stays deterministic.
claims.why: append_round is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify that append_turn is a convenience over it or that ordering is deterministic.

claims.text: Chain the roster accounting: requested / seated / responded / unavailable with machine reasons, plus the DISTINCT INDEPENDENCE CLASS count and a ``degraded`` flag whenever fewer participants responded than were requested.
claims.why: The function builds a record with these fields: requested, seated, responded, unavailable, distinct_classes, degraded. The degraded flag is set to responded < requested.

claims.text: Counts are DERIVED here, never accepted from the caller: "3 of 4" and "2 of 2" must not be able to render as the same string, and a consumer that shows the participant count instead of the distinct-class count is showing a council of clones as a council.
claims.why: Counts are computed from the norm list (requested = len(norm), seated, responded, unavailable, distinct_classes = len(set(heard_classes))). Not accepted from caller.

claims.text: Duplicate weights are detected over everyone SEATED (that is when the clone was let in); the distinct-class count is over those who actually RESPONDED, because an unavailable participant contributes no voice and a class count that includes it overstates the independence on the record.
claims.why: seated_classes includes 'seated', 'responded', 'refused'; heard_classes only includes 'responded'. distinct_classes is len(set(heard_classes)). Duplicate detection uses seated_classes.

claims.text: Read all records, skipping a torn tail line (never fatal). Missing is [].
claims.why: The function body is not provided in this chunk; cannot verify behavior.

observations.what: append_turn calls append_round which is not defined in this chunk; relies on external definition.
append_roster uses several undefined symbols: _reject_unknown, _ACTOR_RE, _ALLOWED_PARTICIPANT_KEYS, PARTICIPANT_OUTCOMES, _norm_class, _norm_strs, _scan_roster, _chain_records.
load_transcript has no implementation; only a stub.
The 'refused' key is set to the return of _scan_roster; if _scan_roster returns a non-dict, the record shape changes.
